To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the use of local radiotherapy to the breast and chest wall in patients with primary breast cancer with synchronous metastatic disease is associated with improved local control, reduced risk of chest wall recurrence and improved overall survival.

the majority of patients with primary breast cancer and synchronous metastatic disease are not candidates for local radiotherapy to the breast and chest wall, but a subset of patients with limited synchronous metastatic disease may be suitable candidates.
